items.title: Can Strategic Acquisitions Strengthen TransDigm's Growth?
items.summary: TDG is expanding its proprietary aerospace portfolio through disciplined acquisitions that bolster aftermarket capabilities and long-term growth.

items.title: Can the Sea-Launched Cruise Missile Program Boost GD's Growth?
items.summary: General Dynamics' $194.1M Navy contract strengthens its role in sea-launched cruise missile support and adds visibility into future strategic defense revenues.

items.title: Redwire Climbs 14.3% in Six Months: Is the Stock Still a Buy?
items.summary: RDW expands its space and defense portfolio as backlog grows, but continued losses and contract execution risks cloud its outlook.

items.title: ‘Some of These Lasers Were the Size of Buildings’: Now They Need 12 Minerals China Cut Off
items.summary: China just restricted 12 minerals that defense contractors need to build the next generation of laser weapons, and Raytheon's $289 billion backlog may be sitting on a supply chain fault line nobody wants to talk about.

items.title: How Long Would You Wait For GE Aerospace Stock To Come Back?
items.summary: GE Aerospace (GE) stock trades at about $329.50, about 14% below the $381.22 high it set inside the past year, and most of the decline is recent. It has fallen 12.7% over the past month. In July the company raised its 2026 guidance across the board.

items.title: Should You Buy Boeing Stock While It Still Loses Money On Airplanes?
items.summary: Boeing (BA) trades at $208.87, down 12.0% over the past twelve months while the S&P 500 returned 20.5%. The complaint behind it is simple: the company still loses money building airplanes. What complicates it is how fast that loss is shrinking.

items.title: Should You Care That Lockheed Martin's Buyback Effect Is Fading?
items.summary: Lockheed Martin (LMT) has spent the past three years handing its owners a slightly bigger slice of the company each year, and the arithmetic worked. Earnings per share grew faster than net income. The stock now sits well below its 52-week high, which makes the question worth asking again: is that quiet compounding still running at the speed the record suggests.

items.title: RTX (RTX) Stock Looks Below Fair Value On Cash Flow, Near Fair Value On Earnings
items.summary: RTX stock has delivered a very strong 5 year run, yet current valuation checks send a mixed message, with a Discounted Cash Flow (DCF) view pointing to some undervaluation while market multiples look closer to fair. Recent contract wins in defense and aerospace add fresh context to that gap between price and intrinsic value estimates.
